 We’ve rounded up the best MagSafe, Qi2, Qi2.2 25W, and MagSafe-compatible magnetic chargers, from the plain pad to multi-functional stands (up to six devices charged), and even the most colorful—from snap-on chargers and modular stands to foldable power banks and full charging desk mats.
 Apple’s MagSafe technology, supported by all models of iPhone since the iPhone 12 (except the iPhone SE and 16e), presents a more efficient way of wirelessly charging compatible iPhones. MagSafe is the ring of magnets around the iPhone’s internal charging coil that senses compatible accessories and magnetically snaps securely into the most efficient charging position with the right accessories. With MagSafe, you’re less likely to wake up to find your phone wasn’t correctly placed on the wireless charger so didn’t charge at all!

 Testing the best for you
 We have tested a lot of magnetic chargers—MagSafe, Qi2 and Compatible—and here inform you which one will work best for you. There are simple magnetic wireless chargers, multi-device chargers for iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods, travel chargers, car chargers and more. 
 Best simple MagSafe chargers 
 Best 2-in-1 MagSafe chargers 
 Best 3-in-1 MagSafe chargers 
 Best 4-in-1 MagSafe Chargers 
 Best travel MagSafe chargers 
 Best MagSafe charging stands with power banks 
 Best MagSafe car charger 
 Best wireless charging desk mat 
 Best wireless charging sleeve 
 Offering up to 25W power output in the right configuration, MagSafe charging is much faster than basic 7.5W magnetic wireless charging. The similar magentic Qi2 standard , supported by the iPhone 13-17 families (and unofficially the iPhone 12 but strangely not the latest 16e) offers similar 15W speed charging. Qi 2.2 , also known as Qi2 25W, meets MagSafe at 25W for iPhone 16/17 series.
 MagSafe or Qi2 certification
 Apple certifies MagSafe accessories to ensures that the output charging is 15W for most iPhones, and up to 25W for iPhone 16 and 17 (with Apple’s latest MagSafe charger or chargers certified for Qi2 25W). Non-certified magnetic but “MagSafe-compatible” chargers are usually just 7.5W with a ring of magnets to hold your phone in place. Certified MagSafe chargers also have a single-wire NFC antenna that allows the iPhone to identify the device and a built-in magnetometer to prevent compass interference while you are using your iPhone while it’s charging.
 In our tests, 15W MagSafe and Qi2 chargers are evenly matched for charging speeds. 7.5W MagSafe compatible chargers, as you might expect, take around twice as long—certainly in the early stages of charging. But don’t rule out 7.5W chargers as they are often high quality, nearly always noticeably cheaper and just take a while longer to fully charge an iPhone. The king of the hill is Apple’s new MagSafe charger and chargers based on the new Qi2 25W technology that are definitely faster at 25W, but only with iPhone 16 or later.
 Foundry
 Simple vs multi-device magnetic chargers
 The most basic form of MagSafe or magnetic charger is the simple pad that latches on to the compatible iPhone. Some pads feature a pop-out arm so the iPhone can be propped up while charging. There are also products that can simultaneously charge an iPhone plus other Apple devices, such as an Apple Watch or wireless AirPods charging case. Note that the AirPods case must be of the wireless variety, and the original AirPods case lacked this functionality. The base of a multi-charger could also be used to charge a second iPhone but mostly not magnetically and at 5W rather than 7.5W, 15W, or 25W. Also see our round up of the Best Apple Watch chargers and stands .
 Best simple MagSafe chargers
 A simple MagSafe charging pad is the cheapest route to wireless iPhone charging. If you are going to the bother of connecting this product to a wall charger, why not just use a Lightning (iPhone 14 or earlier) or USB-C (iPhone 15 and up) cable direct to the iPhone? You can fast-charge an iPhone to 50% battery in under 30 minutes using a cable and just over that using a 25W charger, while it takes around 50 minutes to wirelessly charge iPhone from 0 to 50% using even 15W MagSafe.
 That said, there are interesting options to choose from. After these we’ll look at more multi-functional MagSafe chargers.

 The most obvious MagSafe Charger to buy for your Apple iPhone is, of course, the Apple MagSafe Charger . It’s the charger that Apple would have shipped with the iPhone if it did such things anymore. It’s as minimalist a design as you’d expect from Apple–it looks a lot like a giant Apple Watch Charger. You can also use it to charge your AirPods.
 Apple’s latest version of this charger offers 15W Qi2 support and, more importantly, a faster 25W charging speed with iPhone 16 and later. It also added a 2-meter length option for $10/£10 more, which is very welcome. At least a 30W USB-C power adapter is required for 25W charging.
 In our tests using the Apple MagSafe Charger we wirelessly powered up an iPhone 16 Pro from 0% to 50% in just over 30 minutes.
 It can also charge your AirPods case (AirPods 2 or AirPods Pro), although not at the same time as the iPhone—for that, you’ll need at least a 2-in-1 wireless charger.
 The standard 1m cable is too short to comfortably charge and use your iPhone at the same time, or maybe stretch from a power socket to a nearby table, so we recommend the 2m upgrade. Don’t forget that this Apple charger still requires a USB-C power adapter —at least 20W if you want 15W charging and at least 30W to enable 25W charging.

 If you’re leaving your home in 20 minutes and need as much juice as possible, plug in a cable (USB-C for iPhone 15 or later, or Lightning for earlier iPhones) into a USB-C charger (of at least 30W) to power up an iPhone faster than wireless. With 25W wireless chargers you can simply place your iPhone on and know you should be able to charge it to 50% in around 30 minutes.

Qi2 vs. MagSafe: Which wireless charger is best for your iPhone? | Macworld 
 When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. This doesn't affect our editorial independence .
 by Simon Jary 
 Contributor, Macworld 
 Updated 
 Qi2 vs. MagSafe: Which wireless charger is best for your iPhone?
 Updated 
 Oct 21, 2026 
 Summary created by Smart Answers AI 
 In summary:
 Macworld compares Qi2 and MagSafe wireless charging standards, explaining how both support up to 15W for iPhone 12 through 15, while newer iPhone 16 models can reach 25W via the latest Qi2.2 standard.
 Qi2 chargers match MagSafe speeds without expensive Apple certification fees, making them a more affordable option with broad compatibility across iPhone and Android devices.
 Matching your iPhone model to the correct charger standard appears essential for achieving maximum wireless charging efficiency.
 Not having to find the right cable or carry one around with you makes wireless charging a convenient way of charging your mobile devices—iPhone, Apple Watch, AirPods and many third-party gadgets.
 There are multiple wireless charging standards and technologies. Here we will explain the major ones— Qi , MagSafe , Qi2 and the latest Qi2 25W (aka Qi2.2 ). Knowing which is which will help you to make your charging life more efficient. Here we look at Qi2 vs MagSafe and Qi2 25W vs Qi2 and Apple’s updated 2024 version of MagSafe. Which is best for your model of iPhone?
 It’s a little more nuanced, but in general, iPhones 16, 17 and 18 (and the iPhone Duo) should now charge wirelessly at up to 25W with supporting certified Qi 2.2 chargers. Older iPhones are limited to the 15W maximum if they support certified Apple MagSafe or Qi2. Chargers that are merely “MagSafe Compatible” are usually limited to 7.5W wireless charging. Note that the iPhone Air is limited to 20W wireless, the 16e to 7.5W and 17e to 15W.
 iPhone wireless charging speeds in brief: 
 iPhone 8-11 series and 16e: Qi 7.5W . 0-50% in around 90 minutes.
 iPhone 12-15 series and 17e: MagSafe 15W and Qi2 15W . 0-50% in around 45 minutes.
 iPhone Air: 20W Qi2 . 0-50% in around 40 minutes.
 iPhone 16 and 16 Pro: MagSafe 22W and Qi2.2 22W . 0-50% in around 35 minutes.
 iPhone 16 Plus, 17, 17/18 Pro, 16/17/18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo: MagSafe 25W and Qi2.2 25W . 0-50% in around 30 minutes.
 Don’t worry too much about the difference between 22W and 25W—the charging time difference will be marginal given environmental conditions such as room temperature will also make an impact.
 How does wireless charging work?
 Wireless charging uses electromagnetic induction to power your devices. The charging pad and your phone both include copper wire coils. Plug the pad into a power source and the charger’s coil generates a magnetic field. When you place your phone onto the charging pad, the phone’s coil converts that magnetic field into an electric current, thus charging the phone.
 Apple pioneered improved magnetic connection between charger and phone with MagSafe, and it’s mainly the tighter magnetic fit that drives faster and faster wireless charging.
 What is Qi2? 
 Qi2—supported by the iPhone 12 and up—speeds up wireless charging from 7.5W to 15W and makes chargers cheaper as well as more efficient. It is very like MagSafe, which is unsurprising as Apple allowed the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC) to use MagSafe as the basis of Qi2.
 In short, Qi2 brings the magnetic benefits of MagSafe, but also make third-party iPhone chargers faster and potentially cheaper. Manufacturers are more likely to create new products when the market is larger (iPhone and Android) and costs should come down, too.
 Apple’s latest version of its iPhone MagSafe Charger can wirelessly charge the iPhone 16 series at 22-25W. Older iPhones can use this charger but at a 15W maximum as before. Qi2 took its time catching up, but it has now: keep reading.
 We have tested Qi2 chargers vs chargers certified as MagSafe by Apple, and can confirm that 15W Qi2 charges supporting devices at an equivalent speed to 15W MagSafe, and much faster than merely MagSafe-compatible 7.5W chargers. More details of our wireless charging speed tests below.
 Belkin first announced two Qi2 magnetic wireless charging devices in September 2023. Belkin
 What is Qi2.2 25W?
 The latest Qi2 25W standard (officially Qi 2.2) matches Apple’s 25W wireless charging speed. We have tested many 25W chargers, including the Belkin 25W UltraCharge Pro 3-in-1 Magnetic Charging Dock , Ugreen MagFlow Power Bank , 25W Baseus PicoGo AM52 Power Bank and ESR’s 25W CryoBoost 3-in-1 Charging Station among others.
 Samsung waited until its Galaxy S26 Ultra to jump on the fast magnetic wireless charging bandwagon with Qi2 25W, and Google was first out of the Android blocks with Qi2 25W compatibility with its Pixel 10 Pro XL . The lesser Google Pixel 10 Pro is pegged back at 15W Qi2. Google calls its version of Qi2 “PixelSnap”.
 Wireless charging from Qi to Qi2.2
 First, let’s look at the original Qi, which all iPhones post iPhone 8 support.
 Foundry
 What is Qi wireless charging?
 Qi is a Chinese word that means “energy flow”. Pronounced “chee”, Qi is the basic and most popular wireless charging standard, launched in 2008 but not seen on an iPhone until 2017’s iPhone 8.
 Note that plain Qi2 has little magnetic connection between phone and charger so is less efficient at transferring power as more is wasted depending on the placement of the phone on the charger. Better magnetic attachment and therefore faster charging arrived with MagSafe and Qi2.
 Apple continues to support the Qi wireless charging standard with its most recent iPhones—and the iPhone 12 and later models are compatible with Qi2, more on which later. This means that iPhones from the iPhone 8 onwards can be placed on a Qi-compatible charger to start charging without a cable. (Of course, the Qi charging pad or stand itself has to be connected via a cable to a power charger.)
 While wireless charging means less wear and tear to your devices, it is not as efficient as charging via a cable (wired charging) as some of the energy is lost between the charging pad and the device placed on it.
 Qi users will know that you have to ensure your device is placed in exactly the right alignment for fast wireless charging to take place. Place the iPhone on the pad incorrectly and you end up either charging much more slowly or not at all. Many of us have dropped a phone on a Qi charger only to find out later that it wasn’t in the right place and so annoyingly never started charging—a problem largely solved by Apple’s MagSafe.
 While Qi’s maximum wireless charge is 15W, Apple’s iPhone supports only 7.5W via Qi.
 Which iPhones use Qi? 
 Qi charging is built into the iPhone 8, X, XR, XS, SE, 11, 12, 13, and 14 families. The iPhone 15/16/17/18 and Air/Duo work with Qi but are rated as Qi2; see later. The outlier is the curious iPhone 16e that goes all the way back to plain old Qi; the 17e is fine.
 Foundry
 What is MagSafe wireless charging?
 Apple’s magnetic MagSafe iPhones contain a ring of magnets built around its Qi charging coil. As a result, you can magnetically clamp charging accessories onto the iPhone. In fact, you can magnetically attach non-charging accessories, such as wallets and mounts, too.
 MagSafe—from 2020’s iPhone 12 on—makes missing the charging pad’s coils much less likely with its ring of magnets quickly finding the charging alignment sweet spot—on a compatible charger—so you will always connect and less energy is wasted.
 Magnetic Power Profile (MPP) technology uses magnets to perfectly align the coils of the wireless charging transmitter and receiver before transferring power.
 iPhones can work with wireless chargers that are either MagSafe certified by Apple (“made for MagSafe”) or are compatible with MagSafe—plus less sophisticated Qi chargers.
 Certified MagSafe chargers can supply up to 25W to the iPhone, while merely MagSafe compatible chargers are limited to 7.5W , but compatible chargers are usually cheaper. That 25W charging speed is currently limited to the iPhone 16 and 17 ranges and Apple’s own MagSafe Charger . iPhones 12/13/14/15 max out at 15W using MagSafe. The iPhone Air won’t charge faster than 20W wirelessly. In fact, the iPhone 16 and 16 Pro are pegged back at 22W, while the larger 16 Plus and 16 Pro Max support the while 25W. The 16e is out of the picture at just 7.5W and the 17e makes it to 15W. 
 (Note that the iPhone 12 mini only charges at 12W with MagSafe.)
 We have tested the best MagSafe chargers for iPhones and the best MagSafe power banks for iPhones. This reviews roundup now also includes 15W Qi2 and 25W Qi2.2 chargers as they arrive to market.
 Some thicker cases get in the way of MagSafe wireless charging so make sure your iPhone’s case is MagSafe compatible—see our roundup of the best iPhone 15 Cases , best iPhone 16 cases , best iPhone 17 cases and best iPhone 18 cases .
 Wireless charging is great, but it’s not as fast as wired charging. For truly fast iPhone charging, use a cable connected to at least a 20W USB-C charger. For the iPhone 15 and later that means a USB-C to USB-C cable ; for older iPhones you’ll need a USB-C to Lightning cable . A USB-A to Lightning cable won’t offer iPhone fast charging. Click here for more iPhone fast-charging tips .
 Somewhat confusingly, MagSafe is also the name for Apple’s wired-charging standard for its MacBooks—connecting the charging cable to the MacBook’s MagSafe port via magnets, meaning it is not only easy to connect but, if accidentally disconnected, it pops out rather than dragging your laptop to the floor. This version of MagSafe is magnetic and safe and has a charging connection for MacBooks but is not wireless. We explain the difference between MagSafe on Mac and MagSafe on iPhones in our Complete guide to Apple MagSafe: What is MagSafe? 
 Which iPhones use MagSafe? 
 MagSafe wireless charging is built into the iPhone 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17, and 18 families, with the exception of the 16e. It’s also supported by the iPhone Air and iPhone Duo.
 Foundry
 What is Qi2 wireless charging?
 Qi2 (“chee too”) is the latest version of the Qi “energy flow” wireless charging standard, and it’s supported by all iPhones from the iPhone 12.
 Famed for its “Not Invented Here” strategy, Apple can be quite precious about adopting other technical standards. It has a long history of rejecting any idea that didn’t originate within Apple itself. However, thankfully Apple has cooperated with the creation of Qi2 to the extent that in effect it gave the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC) MagSafe to use as the basis for Qi2’s Magnetic Power Profile that defines how the new generation Qi works. Apple is a WPC “steering member” and chair of the board of directors.
 So what is Qi2 and why is it so great?
 Think of Qi2 as not just MagSafe for Android, but MagSafe benefits for all compatible wireless charging products.
 Qi2 means chargers won’t have to be certified by Apple to support 15W charging. They should, however, meet the technical demands of the WPC. In short, a Qi2 charger will deliver twice as fast charging as “MagSafe-compatible” chargers.
 As MagSafe certification costs manufacturers a fee to Apple, removing this should result in cheaper chargers that match Apple-certified chargers in terms of speed. 
 Which iPhones use Qi2? 
 Qi2 wireless charging works with all iPhones 12. and onwards, except the 16e.
 Simon Jary / Foundry
 What is Qi2 25W wireless charging?
 Qi2 25W is the latest version of the Qi “energy flow” wireless charging standard. Its technical name is Qi2.2.
 It started rolling out in wireless charging products from the mid-2025 and is now seen in many new wireless charging products.
 So what is Qi2 25W and why is it so great?
 Qi2 25W means chargers can support up to 25W wireless charging. They have to meet the technical demands of the WPC. In short, a Qi2 25W charger will deliver 10W more power than Qi2 and 3.3 times as fast charging as MagSafe-compatible chargers.
 The use of a Magnetic Power Profile (MPP) provides better alignment but also reduces magnetic field leakage caused by misalignment. This minimizes the build-up of heat and ensures optimal charging efficiency. A ±0.5mm magnetic alignment precision improves charging efficiency by “up to 40%”, according to manufacturer Baseus.
 Qi2 25W products also feature next-generation thermal regulation with stricter 40°C surface limits and enhanced coil layouts. This ensures that less energy is wasted and provides 15% better charging efficiency—even in motion or with slight misalignment.
 Which iPhones use Qi2 25W?
 Qi2 25W wireless charging will work with the iPhone 16 family and later (except the 16e and 17e). The iPhone Air supports Qi2 25W but only up to 20W, which is likely caused by the super-thin phone’s thermal management. The iPhone 16 and 16 Pro can make it to only 22W according to Apple. The iPhone Duo does support 25W Qi2.2.
 For Qi2 25W to work at full 25W supporting iPhones must have installed at least iOS 26 or later.
 Which is best MagSafe, Qi2 or Qi2 25W?
 First, MagSafe, Qi2 and Qi2 25W are all better than plain Qi. Owing in large part to their magnetic connection, they are more efficient and definitely offer faster wireless charging than Qi.
 For all extents and purposes, Qi2 looks pretty identical to MagSafe so iPhone 12/13/14/15 users can choose between MagSafe or Qi2 without fear. iPhone 16/17/18/Air/Duo owners, however, should look to MagSafe or Qi2 25W, as Apple’s own MagSafe Charger and soon Qi2 25W chargers can reach charging speeds of up to 25W when paired with the latest range of iPhones.
 All should clamp chargers magnetically to the iPhone in the same way and allow for between 15W and 25W wireless charging.
 Will Qi2 chargers work with MagSafe?
 Although technically very similar, Apple is likely to still require MagSafe certification for non-Qi2 products to reach 15W wireless charging. Both the charger and the device must be certified for Qi2 for it to work at 15W, in the same way as MagSafe. However, it is likely that future MagSafe-certified products will also be certified for Qi2, and post iOS 17.2 all iPhones (except 16e) will work natively with Qi2 and Qi2.2 chargers.
 For consumers it’s a win-win as Qi2 and Qi2 25W means faster wireless charging will be brought to more devices and people. For product marketers it may be a bit of a labelling nightmare until all the chargeable devices catch up with the technology: expect MagSafe Compatible (7.5W), MagSafe (15W or 25W), Qi2 15W (15W) and Qi2 25W or Qi2.2 (25W).
 Is Qi2 as fast at wireless charging as MagSafe?
 As the Wireless Power Consortium used Apple technology to build the Qi2 specification, it is true that Qi2 matches MagSafe for speed. Both can charge at up to 15W and use the largely same magnetic attachment tech. Note the 25W charging potential of the Apple MagSafe Charger and iPhone 16/17, plus the same charging speed from Qi2 25W.
 The first Qi2 charger we tested and reviewed at Macworld was the Anker MagGo 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Station . We tested its Qi2 wireless charging speed by charging an iPhone 15 Pro all the way to a 100% full charge, and taking timings at 30%, 50% and 80%. We did the same using a Apple’s own MagSafe Charger and also via a straight wired USB-C connection.
 The fastest way to charge an iPhone is via a wired connection: USB-C to Lightning for iPhones older than the iPhone 15, and USB-C to USB-C for the iPhone 15 and later. The average wired-charging time in our tests was 25 minutes to 50%, 55 minutes to 80% and 70 minutes to 100%.
 Our wireless charging tests for officially Apple-certified MagSafe chargers (using Apple’s own Wireless Charger) and for Qi2 magnetic wireless charging (using the Anker MagGo) had remarkably similar timings. There was some variance either way but also small differences using the same charger so we are confident that using these two magentic wireless charging technologies came up with the same basic results on average: 45 minutes to 50%, 90 minutes to 80% and 115 minutes to 100%. 
 In summary, then, MagSafe and Qi2 charging at 15W results in the same times and so can be considered equal—except for the 25W MagSafe potential of the iPhone 16/17–and the same from Qi2 25W now it is released. And, again as expected, merely MagSafe-compatible chargers took twice as long as the 15W chargers: 45 minutes to 30%, and 90 minutes to 50%.
 Our tests demonstate that Qi2 25W will charges an iPhone 16 Pro from 0–50% in just over 30 minutes—manufacturers often claim 25 minutes but that is under clinical conditions. In Macworld’s real-world tests 32-34 minutes is the average. In comparison, a Qi2 15W charger generally takes about 45 minutes to reach the same level—this would work out as the 25W option being around 45% faster than the 15W chargers. Wireless charging depends on many factors, such as device settings, usage during charging, and ambient temperature.
 Don’t concern yourself greatly about the 22W limit of the iPhone 16 and 16 Pro. The 3% difference between that and 25W is marginal.
 Why does phone charging speed slow down as the battery gets fuller?
 Batteries charge slower the fuller they get, especially in the last 10–20% of charging. The fuller the battery is, the slower it absorbs energy.
 To start with, a Lithium-Ion battery accepts whatever current it can, but as the battery gets closer to being full it accepts less current, and so the power being transferred tapers off.
 Imagine you were filling up a glass with water. You can start with the faucet or tap at full blast, but as the glass gets fuller, you have to slow the flow down to avoid the water spilling over, until eventually just a trickle of water goes in as you try to get it right up to the brim.
 If the battery didn’t charge this way and instead filled up at full blast till reaching 100%, it would get very hot and you’d risk damaging it to the point it might explode!
 Slowing down the charge when the battery is getting closer to full also increases the number of charge cycles a battery can go through before it permanently loses capacity.
 Taking advantage of this, if you need to charge quickly, stop at 80%, use the device for a while and then top back up to 80% before the charging speed starts to slow.
 Ugreen

 1 . Best Overall
 UGREEN MagFlow Qi2.2 25W Wireless Charging Pad
 BeastScore 92 / 100 Typically $25–$35 on Amazon (checked October 30, 2026 ) 
 This is the charger most people should buy. The listing says up to 25W for the iPhone 17 series, roughly 50% in 30 minutes on the Pro Max, with a 5 ft cable and a pad that weighs under 3 oz. It snaps on with magnets, so you can use your phone while it charges. It does not include a power adapter. UGREEN says you need 45W or higher for best results, so add a USB-C charger if you do not own one. The listing is written for iPhone and AirPods and says charging other brands is not recommended.
 Pros
 Lists 25W Qi2.2 for the iPhone 17 series
 Light and compact enough for a bag
 Low price for a Qi2.2 charger
 Cons
 No power adapter in the box
 Made for iPhone: UGREEN does not recommend other brands
 No stand and no fan, so it can warm up

 This is the pick if you want a stand and a fan in one small pad. ESR says the CryoBoost fan keeps temperatures down and runs under 25 dB, and the stand tilts from 0 to 150 degrees for portrait or landscape. ESR is one of the few listings that names Samsung S25/S26 and Pixel phones as compatible , though a magnetic case may still be needed on Galaxy phones. No adapter comes in the box. The ESR lab figures are the maker’s own claims, so treat them as such.

The adapter is not included and the listing advises a PD adapter of 30W or more. It has fewer owner reviews than the big names, so expect less proof of long-term durability. For a spare charger at the office or in a guest room, it is hard to beat.

Samsung phones do not have magnets inside, so a magnetic case is how you get the snap-on hold . The speed a Galaxy gets depends on the model, and sources differ, so treat 25W as the charger’s ceiling, not a promise. It includes a 45W adapter. The watch charger is not included: you add your own into the built-in holder.

 Quick tips before you buy
 25W needs three things
 A Qi2.2 charger, a phone that supports 25W (iPhone 16 and newer on iOS 26, or the Pixel 10 Pro XL), and a 35W to 45W adapter.
 Buy the adapter
 Most pads here ship without one. A weak adapter is the top reason a 25W pad charges at 15W.
 Android needs magnets
 All Pixel 10 phones have magnets built in. Galaxy phones need a magnetic case to snap on. Without it you get no alignment.
 Cooling keeps speed up
 Phones slow down when hot. A fan or TEC cooler helps in cars and on warm desks, at the cost of a faint hum.
 Quick answers
 What does Qi2 mean? + Qi2 is the newer Qi wireless charging standard from the Wireless Power Consortium. It adds a ring of magnets so the phone lines up with the charger, like MagSafe. Original Qi2 charges at up to 15W. Qi2.2 raises that ceiling to 25W.
 Is Qi2 the same as MagSafe? + They are close. Apple’s MagSafe was the base for Qi2, and a Qi2 charger works with iPhone 12 and newer. Qi2 is an open standard that other brands can use. Apple’s own 25W MagSafe speeds need iOS 26 and a phone that supports it.
 Do I need a Qi2.2 charger to get 25W? + Yes. A Qi2 15W charger cannot go past 15W. You also need a phone that supports 25W and a 35W to 45W USB-C adapter. Many chargers in this guide do not include one, so check the listing.
 Does Qi2 work on the Pixel 10? + Yes. Google says all Pixel 10 models have Qi2 magnets built in. Google lists up to 15W for the Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold, and up to 25W for the Pixel 10 Pro XL with a stronger adapter.
 Does Qi2 work with Samsung Galaxy phones? + Yes, in a limited way. Sources differ by model, with the S26 Ultra listed at 25W by some brands and other Galaxy phones at 15W or less. Galaxy phones do not have magnets inside, so you need a Qi2 magnetic case for the snap-on hold. Check the charger’s per-model speed table before you buy.
 Will an iPhone 15 or older charge at 25W? + No. UGREEN and Belkin list 15W for iPhone 12 to 15. The 25W figure is for newer iPhones, and the iPhone 16 needs iOS 26 or later.
 What is the best Qi2 charger for travel? + The UGREEN MagFlow 25W Pocket-Sized Foldable. It is 3.88 oz and folds flat. Remember it is not a battery, so it must stay plugged in. For a power bank, the Anker MagGo 10,000mAh is the slim option, but it is optimized for iPhones.

 Best Qi2 Wireless Chargers in 2026 — Qi2 vs Qi2.2 25W Ranked
 Daniel Bartet · USB-C Research Specialist · Updated April 2026 · 10 min read 
 Wireless charging moved fast in the last year. The original Qi2 standard (15W) is now joined by Qi2.2 at 25W — the new top speed available on iPhone 17, iPhone 16, iPhone 15, and Google Pixel 10. And the form factor that's actually selling and ranking in 2026 isn't single pads anymore — it's 3-in-1 stations that charge your phone, Apple Watch, and AirPods from one cable.
 We compared the leading Qi2 and Qi2.2 chargers across both standards (15W and 25W) and ranked the five best for different use cases — overall best, premium with cooling, value 3-in-1, compact, and 2-in-1 for users without AirPods. All five are Qi2 or Qi2.2 certified, with full magnetic alignment. Learn more about how Qi2 works .
 Quick Answer: What Is the Best Qi2 Wireless Charger?
 The Spigen ArcField Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 foldable is the best Qi2 wireless charger for most people in 2026 — it delivers the new Qi2.2 25W speed for iPhone 17/16/15, charges all three Apple daily devices, and folds flat for travel. For maximum sustained 25W speed at a desk, the ESR HaloLock CryoBoost adds active cooling to prevent throttling. If you don't need Qi2.2 25W, the Anker MagGo Foldable Qi2 15W is the best value 3-in-1. For users without AirPods, the Belkin Qi2.2 25W 2-in-1 is the slimmest fast option.
 Qi2 vs Qi2.2 — Which One Do You Actually Need?
 The wireless charging standard you can use depends on your phone, not the charger. Qi2.2 chargers are backward-compatible — they charge Qi2 phones at 15W and standard Qi phones at 5–10W. So buying Qi2.2 is never wrong, but you only get the 25W benefit if your phone supports it.
 Which standard your phone uses
 Qi2.2 (25W): iPhone 17, iPhone 16, iPhone 15 (all variants), Google Pixel 10. 
 Qi2 (15W): iPhone 12, 13, 14; Samsung Galaxy S24 and later; Google Pixel 8 and 9; select Motorola, Xiaomi, and OnePlus flagships. 
 Standard Qi (5–10W): Older iPhones and most pre-2024 Android phones. Still work on Qi2/Qi2.2 chargers at standard speed. 
 The honest take: for overnight charging, 15W vs 25W makes zero practical difference. Both finish a full charge with hours to spare. The 25W advantage is real only for daytime top-ups — if you regularly need to add 30% in 15 minutes, Qi2.2 25W matters. Otherwise, save money on a Qi2 15W charger and put it toward something else. See also our deeper comparison of wireless vs wired charging , and if you're worried about battery health, here's what the evidence actually says .

 The Spigen ArcField is our top overall pick because it nails the three things that matter most right now: it delivers Qi2.2 25W (the new high-speed standard introduced in 2025), it covers all three Apple daily-carry devices, and it folds flat for travel. Most 3-in-1 stations are bulky bedside fixtures; the Spigen is the rare one you can throw in a backpack. For anyone upgrading their wireless charging setup in 2026, this is the straightforward correct answer.

 What to Look for When Buying a Qi2 Wireless Charger in 2026
 1. Qi2 or Qi2.2 — Match Your Phone
 If you own an iPhone 17, 16, or 15 (or Pixel 10), Qi2.2 25W is the faster standard and worth paying for if you do frequent daytime top-ups. If you have an older iPhone or any 2024 Android flagship, Qi2 15W is the cap your phone supports — no point paying extra for Qi2.2.
 2. Thermal Performance for 25W
 Hitting Qi2.2 25W on the spec sheet is easy; sustaining it for 30 minutes is hard. Most chargers throttle to 15–20W after a few minutes when the phone heats up. Active cooling (like ESR's CryoBoost) sustains real 25W much longer. If you only charge overnight, ignore this. If you charge in 15–20 minute bursts during the day, it matters.
 3. Form Factor: Foldable vs Desk vs Compact
 Foldable 3-in-1 (Spigen, Anker Foldable) packs flat — best for travel. Desk 3-in-1 (ESR) has the best build and cooling but is fixed in place. Compact stand (Anker Nano) has the smallest footprint for tight nightstands. Pick based on where the charger actually lives day to day.
 4. Power Adapter Wattage
 For Qi2 15W chargers, a 20W USB-C PD adapter is enough. For Qi2.2 25W, you need a 30W or higher USB-C PD adapter or you'll throttle to ~15W even on a Qi2.2 pad. Wall adapters are usually sold separately — check the listing carefully. Our cable guide covers USB-C cable recommendations.
 5. 2-in-1 vs 3-in-1
 If you don't own AirPods, a 2-in-1 (phone + watch port) is smaller, cheaper, and just as fast on the phone. If you own all three Apple devices, a 3-in-1 eliminates cable clutter and is worth the extra $20-30. Don't buy a 3-in-1 if you'll never use one of the pads.

 Daniel Bartet · USB-C Research Specialist · Updated June 2026 · 10 min read 
 Quick answer: The best power bank for most iPhone 17 owners is the Baseus PicoGo AM52 (Qi2.2, 25W) — it's the fastest cable-free magnetic charger the iPhone 17 supports, at the best price. The Anker MagGo (Qi2, 10,000mAh) is the best-built magnetic pick with a kickstand, the Baseus Qi2 (15W) is the budget ultra-slim option, and the Anker 20,000mAh USB-C is the high-capacity wired pick for heavy users.
 The iPhone 17 and 17 Pro are among the first phones to support Qi2.2 magnetic charging at up to 25W — a real jump over the 15W of Qi2 and Apple's MagSafe. That changes which power bank is worth buying: a magnetic bank now charges meaningfully faster without a cable, while a high-capacity wired bank still wins for raw speed and total charges. This guide covers both, with the exact trade-offs for each pick.
 All four picks below were evaluated for the iPhone 17 specifically: magnetic hold, real-world wireless wattage, capacity (how many full charges you actually get), and how each behaves with a MagSafe-compatible case. No product earns a spot on specs alone.

 iPhone 17 Charging: Qi2, Qi2.2, MagSafe & Wired
 The iPhone 17 supports both magnetic (cable-free) and wired charging. Understanding the three magnetic standards — plus how wired compares — tells you exactly which bank to buy.
 The four ways to charge an iPhone 17
 MagSafe (15W): Apple's magnetic system. Snaps onto the phone, charges at up to 15W. No cable needed. 
 Qi2 (15W): The open industry standard that adopted MagSafe's magnets. Same 15W speed, same snap-on convenience — effectively MagSafe for everyone. 
 Qi2.2 (up to 25W): The newer revision the iPhone 17 supports. Still magnetic and cable-free, but up to 25W — the fastest no-cable option. 
 Wired USB-C (PD): A cable into the iPhone 17's USB-C port. The fastest method overall, but you have to carry and plug in a cable. 
 The practical takeaway: if you want cable-free charging, a Qi2.2 bank (25W) charges your iPhone 17 noticeably faster than a Qi2 or MagSafe bank (15W). If you want the fastest possible charging and the most total charges, a high-capacity wired USB-C bank wins — at the cost of carrying a cable. For more on mixing devices, see can one charger handle a laptop and a phone .
 How Much Capacity Do You Need?
 Capacity is rated in mAh, but you never get all of it — conversion losses (especially over wireless) mean you use roughly 60-70% of the rated number. Here's what that means in full iPhone 17 charges:
 10,000mAh ≈ ~2 full iPhone 17 charges. The everyday-carry sweet spot — slim enough to keep magnetically attached, enough power for a day or two of backup. 
 20,000mAh ≈ ~4 full iPhone 17 charges. For travel, long days, or charging a tablet/laptop too — heavier, and wired-only on our pick. 
 If you also want a bank that can charge a laptop, that's a different tool — see our best USB-C power banks for laptops guide.

 What to Look For in an iPhone 17 Power Bank
 1. Magnetic standard (Qi2 vs Qi2.2)
 If you want cable-free charging, this is the most important spec. Qi2.2 (25W) charges the iPhone 17 faster than Qi2/MagSafe (15W). Only buy a Qi2.2 bank if you want that speed — otherwise a cheaper Qi2 bank is fine.
 2. Capacity vs portability
 10,000mAh (~2 charges) stays slim and magnet-friendly. 20,000mAh (~4 charges) is for travel and heavy use but is bigger and usually wired-only. Match the size to how often you're away from an outlet.
 3. Magnetic hold and case compatibility
 A strong magnet keeps the bank attached while you use the phone. Use a MagSafe/Qi2- compatible case so the magnets align; very thick cases weaken the hold and slow wireless charging.
 4. Extras that matter
 A built-in kickstand (Anker MagGo) is genuinely useful for video. A USB-C PD port lets you charge fastest by cable when you need to, and recharges the bank quickly. An airline- legal capacity (under 100Wh) matters if you fly.

 The best power banks for the iPhone 17 (2026) are: the Baseus PicoGo AM52 (Qi2.2, 25W, 10,000mAh) as the fastest magnetic charger and best value; the Anker MagGo (Qi2, 15W, 10,000mAh) as the best-built magnetic pick with a kickstand; the Baseus MagSafe (Qi2, 15W) as the budget ultra-slim option; and the Anker 20,000mAh USB-C bank as the high-capacity wired pick for heavy users. The iPhone 17 supports Qi2.2 magnetic charging at up to 25W — faster than Qi2/MagSafe's 15W — so a Qi2.2 bank charges fastest without a cable, while wired USB-C remains fastest overall. A 10,000mAh bank delivers about two full iPhone 17 charges; 20,000mAh delivers about four.  How I tested the iPhone chargers in this guide 
 (Image credit: Future) I’ve personally tested every single charger in this guide myself – as well as a number of models that didn’t make the cut, which I’ve listed above.
 I curated this list based on more than 18 months of testing chargers here at TechRadar. During this time, I’ve tested all kinds of models, from tiny wall adapters to large-sized desktop chargers.
 The actual testing process I follow is pretty simple. When my phone hits 0%, I time the amount of time it takes for a charger to get it all the way back to 100%. If a charger has multiple ports, I’ll also test it with all of them in use to ensure they perform well across the board.
 On top of that, I ensure that the primary USB-C cable I use remains the same – the reliable UGreen 240W cable has been my go-to since I began testing chargers.
 Keen to learn more about how we review gadgets at TechRadar? Make sure you head on over to our ' how we test ' guide.
 Q&A: my advice for buying 
 (Image credit: Future) How do I choose the right iPhone charger?
 Of course, it's important to set a budget and decide how much you’re willing to spend on your shiny new charger, but there’s a lot more to consider too. For example – if you regularly upgrade your iPhone, will the wall charger you pick have enough wattage to juice up your future devices? Sure, a 30W model may suit an iPhone 15, but if you’re going to upgrade to the iPhone 17 Pro, you’ll be better off with a 45W model.
 All of the chargers in this guide support USB-C as an absolute minimum, and I’d certainly recommend a model with that – it's the standard for just about every modern Apple device and the rest of the mobile market. It’s also wise to go for USB-C even if you don’t need it right now. Of course, I’m referring to the side of a cable that plugs into your charger here – if you’re using an older iPhone model, then you’ll want to make sure you’ve got a lightning connector on the other end of said cable.
 What’s the difference between wireless and wired charging?
 Wireless isn’t always as fast, but can often feel more convenient. Most wireless iPhone chargers deliver 5W-25W of power, and work through most iPhone cases.
 It’s worth noting, however, that a lot of wireless charging pads come without an actual charger brick, and can’t deliver more power than you put into them. So, even if you had an iPhone wireless charging pad capable of delivering 25W, it can’t do that if you’re plugging it into a charger that only gives it 20W.
 What to look for in an iPhone charger
 This will differ depending on the kind of charger you’re searching for, but the trinity of performance, design, and value for money should apply across the board.
 For a basic wall charger, I personally love when a charger is compact and can easily slide into a pocket or bag – is it relatively small for its power output? Do its prongs fold away? These are the key questions I’ll ask.
 I also need to ensure it has the power output to support my devices. 45W should do for my phone, but my laptop can charge up to 100W, so a model like the UGreen Uno 100W charger suits me to a T. That model is great because it has four ports, so I can also charge my wireless headphones while juicing up my laptop, so the number of ports is a crucial aspect to consider when choosing a new iPhone charger.
 For wireless chargers, you should make sure you know if your iPhone supports wireless charging up to 15W or 25W. If it's the latter, you may need to fork out a fair amount to get peak performance, but no matter what, make sure you connect the wireless charger to a power brick with enough wattage. 
 On top of that, design matters. Want something for your desk? Then a standing design will work best. Want something for handheld use? Perhaps consider a MagSafe model that’s diminutive and comfortable to hold.

 Charging style and daily setup
 Some shoppers want a flat pad, while others need a foldable stand or a 2-in-1 station. Choose the shape that fits your desk, nightstand, or travel bag, and check whether it still charges when folded.
 Power input and included accessories
 Wireless chargers often depend on a separate USB-C power adapter, while some listings include one. Confirm what is in the box so you do not end up with a charger that cannot reach its stated performance.
 Cable length and portability
 A 5-foot or 6-foot cable can make a big difference on a desk, in a hotel room, or next to a bed. If you move between spaces often, a longer cable and a compact body are worth prioritizing.
 Heat control and safety features
 Because wireless charging can create heat, look for temperature management, overcurrent protection, and clear instructions about ventilation. That matters even more if you charge overnight or keep the phone attached for long periods.
 Multi-device convenience
 If you also use AirPods or a smartwatch, a charger with an extra port or a second charging spot may be more practical than a single-pad design. Just verify the supported device types on the current listing.

 What makes a charger a good choice for iPhone 17? 
 Look for Qi2 or MagSafe compatibility, clear iPhone 17 support, and a power setup that matches the listing. It also helps if the charger includes a long cable or a stand style that fits your routine.
 Do I need a special adapter for these chargers? 
 Some listings say a higher-wattage USB-C PD adapter is required, while others include one. Always check the product page so you know what is in the box and what you need to buy separately.
 Will a thick case affect Qi2 charging? 
 It can. Many magnetic chargers work best with a case that supports magnetic alignment, and thicker cases may reduce speed or stability.
 Is a foldable charger better than a flat pad?

 Best 3-in-1 chargers for iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods
 By Luka Anderson 1 November 2026

 Belkin’s Qi2.2 3-in-1 stand charges an iPhone at up to 25W with a compatible iPhone and iOS version
 The foldable Belkin model suits travel and a nightstand that doubles as a bag charger
 Apple’s own chargers are the simplest choice if you only need two devices

 A 3-in-1 charger is one of those accessories that quietly improves every evening. Instead of three cables on the nightstand, your iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods each have a place to sit. It is also one of the most popular Apple-adjacent gifts, which means the category is crowded with lookalikes that charge slowly or wobble.
 The short answer: Belkin’s Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 charging stand is the one to buy for a nightstand or desk. If you travel or want one charger for home and bag, the foldable Belkin model is the better choice. If you only charge an iPhone and a watch, Apple’s own MagSafe and Apple Watch chargers are simpler. These picks are based on published specifications and compatibility, not our own long-term testing.
 Quick picks Belkin Best for a nightstand Belkin Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 charging station, Black View on Amazon 
 Best for travel Belkin Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 foldable charger View on Amazon 
 Apple Best for just an iPhone Apple MagSafe Charger (1 m) View on Amazon 
 First, check what your iPhone can actually do
 The headline 25W only applies when the phone, the charger and the software all support it. Every current flagship from iPhone 16 to iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo can reach 25W with a Qi2.2 or recent MagSafe charger, while iPhone Air tops out at 20W and iPhone 17e at 15W. Belkin notes that its 25W speeds need iOS 26 or newer. Our full list of MagSafe and Qi2 charging speeds covers every model.
 Older iPhones with MagSafe still charge on these stands, just more slowly. iPhone 16e and older SE models have no magnets, so a magnetic stand will not hold them in place. Also use the power adapter in the box or one Belkin specifies; a weak USB-C brick is the most common reason a fast charger feels slow.
 Photo via Apple // iPhone 18 Pro models with Apple cases and a MagSafe charger; iPhone 16 and later can charge at up to 25W with compatible chargers.

 Advertise here 
 Best overall: Belkin Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 Charging Station
 Belkin’s stand holds the iPhone magnetically on an upright arm, with an Apple Watch charger and an AirPods pad below. It charges the phone at up to 25W, the watch quickly enough that Belkin quotes 0 to 80% for an Apple Watch Series 10 in about 45 minutes, and AirPods at up to 5W. It has a weighted chrome base and a small fan with an on/off switch that runs only when a device is attached. That fan is what lets it keep charging fast without overheating.
 The one to buy for a nightstand or desk Belkin Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 charging station, Black A weighted nightstand stand that charges iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods together, with a fan for 25W speeds. Qi2.2 up to 25W Active cooling fan Apple Watch fast charging StandBy Check price on Amazon 
 Two caveats. First, a fan can make a light hum, which Belkin itself acknowledges. If you are a light sleeper, use the switch, accept slower charging overnight, or choose the passively cooled foldable model. Second, it is a large object for a small nightstand. Measure first if space is tight.
 The stand works with StandBy, which turns a charging iPhone on its side into a clock, photo frame or widget display. That is one of the best reasons to choose an upright stand over a flat pad.
 Best for travel: Belkin Qi2.2 25W Foldable 3-in-1
 The foldable model packs flat for a bag and still charges the iPhone at up to 25W, with Belkin quoting 0 to 50% in about 29 minutes. The stand angle adjusts up to 65 degrees for portrait or landscape, and the iPhone can still charge while the stand is folded. It uses passive cooling, so there is no fan to hear.
 For travel, or one charger for home and bag Belkin Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 foldable charger Charges an iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods from one stand, and folds for travel. Qi2.2 25W 3 devices Foldable Check price on Amazon 
 The trade-off is stability. A folding stand is lighter and easier to knock over than a weighted base, and passive cooling means it can slow down sooner in a warm room. For a hotel room or a second desk, it is the more useful design.

 The latest Apple news, leaks, and wallpapers — once a month, no spam.
 We respect your privacy and won’t share your email.
 Photo via Macworld // MagSafe and Qi2 chargers look alike; the certification and the phone decide the actual charging speed. 
 If you only charge two devices: Apple’s chargers
 A 3-in-1 only earns its space if you use all three spots. Many people charge AirPods rarely, from a USB-C cable or in a case that lasts days. For them, Apple’s own MagSafe Charger and Apple Watch Magnetic Fast Charger are the cleaner setup.
 Apple’s 1m MagSafe Charger for the iPhone Apple MagSafe Charger (1 m) Apple’s own magnetic iPhone charger, for people who only need to charge a phone. MagSafe Up to 25W on supported iPhones 1 m cable Check price on Amazon 
 Apple’s fast charger for Apple Watch Apple Watch Magnetic Fast Charger to USB-C Cable (1 m) Apple’s woven fast charger for Apple Watch, used with a USB-C power adapter. Fast charging USB-C 1 m woven cable Check price on Amazon 
 Apple says its watch charger is fast-charging capable with an Apple 20W USB-C adapter, and quotes, for example, 18 hours of use for Apple Watch Ultra 4 from 15 minutes of charging. You will need two power adapters or a multi-port charger. Our guide to the best USB-C chargers covers compact multi-port bricks that can power both.

 Does your case work with a magnetic stand?
 Thin cases with their own MagSafe magnets work fine. Thick rugged cases, wallets, grips and rings attached to the back of the phone can weaken the magnetic hold or stop charging entirely. If you use a PopSocket-style grip, check whether it is designed to stay on while charging; many need removing.
 Apple Watch bands matter too. Some 3-in-1 stands put the watch charger close to the base, and a closed loop or metal link band may not let the watch lie flat. Stands like Belkin’s with a raised watch puck generally handle open bands better.
 What to skip
 Skip unbranded 3-in-1 stands that do not state Qi2 or Qi2.2 certification. They often use weaker magnets, charge at 7.5W or 15W, and run hot. Skip chargers that use a flat AirPods pad if your AirPods case does not support wireless charging. And skip a 3-in-1 entirely if you will only ever charge your phone on it: a single MagSafe charger is cheaper and takes up less room.

 Product prices and availability are accurate as of the date/time indicated and are subject to change. Any price and availability information displayed on Amazon.com at the time of purchase will apply to the purchase of this product.
 TL;DR
 Top pick: ESR CryoBoost Foldable 3-in-1 ($99.99) — fastest 25W Qi2.2 station, active cooling, iPhone 17 to 60% in 30 min [ src5 , src6 ].
 Best value: Belkin Qi2.2 25W 2-in-1 Foldable ($49.99) — full 25W plus AirPods, 45W adapter included [ src3 ].
 Best budget: UGREEN Qi2 15W Pad ($12.99) — cheapest name-brand Qi2-certified pad [ src10 , src11 ].
 Summary
 Qi2 has split into two clearly separate tiers, and in August 2026 the price gap between them has almost closed. Qi2.2 (branded "Qi2 25W", introduced July 2025) delivers 25W with magnetic alignment; plain Qi2 delivers 15W; anything sold as "Qi2 Ready" is a magnet accessory bolted to a non-Qi2 charger and is not certified at all [ src4 , src11 ]. Apple's iPhone 17 series charges at the full 25W, iPhone 16 does so only on iOS 26 or newer (Belkin states this limit in its own listings), Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra supports 25W while the base S26 is capped at 15W and still needs a magnetic case, and Google's Pixel 10 Pro XL was the first Android phone with built-in magnets [ src4 , src7 ].
 The August 2026 price picture inverted the one from spring. 25W got cheap: Belkin's Qi2.2 25W 2-in-1 Foldable is $59.99 with a 45W adapter in the box (Engadget's best 2-in-1 pick), its 25W 3-in-1 for Android is $64.95, and Spigen's Foldable Qi2.2 25W 2-in-1 is $24.99 [ src3 ]. Meanwhile 15W gear got more expensive: Belkin's 15W BoostCharge Pro 3-in-1 climbed to $89.99, within $10 of full-speed 25W 3-in-1 stations, and UGREEN's MagFlow returned to its $139.99 list price after selling at $99.99 during the spring sale [ src3 ]. The practical consequence: in 2026 there is almost no reason to pay a premium for a 15W multi-device station.
 Two caveats still decide real-world results. First, sustained 25W is short-lived — speeds typically fall to 15W or lower after the first 5-10 minutes as thermal limits are hit, so active cooling (ESR CryoBoost, Anker AirCool at 19 dB) buys minutes, not a different class of performance [ src3 , src4 ]. Second, wattage claims on cheap listings are unreliable: several sub-$15 "Qi2 certified" pads on Amazon come from unbranded sellers, and the only way to confirm a certification is the manufacturer's own spec sheet or the WPC's certified-product database [ src11 ]. Sticking to Anker, Belkin, ESR, UGREEN, Satechi, Spigen, mophie and Twelve South avoids that trap.

 Best for Each Use Case
 Best Overall: ESR CryoBoost Foldable 3-in-1 (25W) ($99.99) — Check price 
 The ESR CryoBoost Foldable 3-in-1 remains the fastest wireless charging in a multi-device station. Its Qi2.2-certified 25W output takes an iPhone 17 or 17 Pro to 60% in 30 minutes per ESR's own listing, and the active CryoBoost cooling fan reduces device temperatures by up to 6.5 degrees F, keeping sustained speeds higher than passive competitors [ src5 , src6 ]. It folds to 4.33 x 2.44 x 0.62 inches, charges iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods simultaneously, and ships with a 50W USB-C wall charger and cable — the bundled brick is worth $25-35 on its own. Verified price 2026-08-05: $99.99. [ src2 , src6 ]
 Best Value 25W: Belkin Qi2.2 25W 2-in-1 Foldable ($59.99) — Check price 
 This is the biggest change on the card since June. Belkin's 2-in-1 foldable delivers the full 25W Qi2.2 to an iPhone (0-50% in 29 minutes), charges AirPods at 5W on the second pad, adds a 5W USB-C port for a watch or a third device, folds flat for travel and includes a 45W adapter — Engadget's pick for best 2-in-1 [ src3 ]. At $59.99 it costs $40 less than the 3-in-1 version and still gets you full-speed charging; the only thing you give up is the dedicated Apple Watch puck. Note Belkin's own caveat: 25W requires iOS 26 or newer. [ src3 ]
 Best 25W with Apple Watch: Belkin Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 Foldable ($99.99) — Check price 
 If you need a genuine fast-charge Apple Watch puck alongside 25W phone charging, Belkin's 3-in-1 foldable is the value route to it: 0-50% on iPhone in 29 minutes, Apple Watch Series 10 from 0-80% in 30 minutes, AirPods at 5W, ChillBoost passive cooling (no fan noise) and a 45W adapter plus a 5-foot cable in the box. It hit a $70 all-time low on the spring sales and sits at $99.99 in August — level with the actively cooled ESR, which is why the ESR keeps the overall pick [ src2 , src8 ].
 Best Premium: Anker Prime 3-in-1 (25W) ($119.99) — Check price 
 Anker's flagship Prime station pairs 25W Qi2.2 with an AirCool fan that Anker rates at just 19 dB — the quietest active cooling here — and a smart display showing charging status. Anker's listing claims an iPhone 17 Pro reaches 50% in 26 minutes. It measures 3.74 x 2.38 x 1.22 inches folded, weighs 8.11 oz, and includes a pop-out Apple Watch charger. List $149.99, $119.99 on Amazon as of 2026-08-05 (-20%). [ src1 , src5 ]
 Best for Samsung/Android: Belkin Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 for Android ($64.95) — Check price 
 Belkin's Android-oriented station delivers 25W to Galaxy, Pixel and other Qi2-compatible phones on the main pad, 5W to earbuds on the second pad, and works with magnetic cases up to 3mm thick — which matters because Samsung phones need a magnetic case for alignment [ src7 ]. The hidden cost to know: the watch cradle takes your own official smartwatch charger, which is NOT included; Belkin supplies only silicone inserts sized for Samsung, Google and Apple watch pucks. If you don't already own a spare watch charger, add $30-60 to the price. [ src3 , src7 ]
 Best Desk Stand: UGREEN MagFlow 3-in-1 (25W) ($139.99) — Check price 
 The MagFlow is still the best-executed desk stand — 25W Qi2.2, 16 magnets for a firm lock, foldable at 7.4 oz, tilt and rotation for FaceTime and StandBy mode, ThermalGuard protection, and a bundled wall adapter and cable (Engadget lists a 45W brick with this model) [ src3 , src4 ]. The catch is the price: it was $99.99 during the spring sale and is back to $139.99 list in August, a 40% swing that makes it the most expensive 3-in-1 here. Buy it on a sale, or take the Belkin 3-in-1 foldable at $99.99 for the same 25W speed. [ src3 ]
 Best Budget 25W: Belkin Qi2 25W Magnetic Pad ($29.99) — Check price 
 The cheapest way from a major brand to get full 25W Qi2.2 to a single device: 0-50% in 31 minutes, a built-in kickstand that doubles as a finger loop, and a tethered 6.6ft USB-C cable. Two things the listing is explicit about and buyers miss: no wall adapter is included, and you need a 30W or higher USB-C PD adapter to actually see 25W. Budget $20-30 for a brick if you don't have one. [ src2 , src3 ]
 Cheapest 25W 2-in-1: Spigen Foldable Qi2.2 2-in-1 (25W) ($24.99) — Check price 
 Spigen's foldable stand is the least expensive 25W Qi2.2 charger on this card at $24.99 — it charges a phone magnetically at up to 25W plus a second device (earbuds or a watch) on the same compact frame, adjusts for portrait or landscape viewing, and adds an extra USB-C port. Spigen sells the same Qi2.2 2-in-1 design at $99.99 on spigen.com, so the Amazon price is the outlier to buy on. No wall adapter is listed in the box; pair it with a 30W+ PD brick for full speed. [ src3 ]
 Best Ultra-Budget: UGREEN Qi2 15W Pad ($16.99) — Check price 
 With ESR's HaloLock Mini line out of stock across Amazon US in August 2026, UGREEN's Qi2-certified 15W pad at $16.99 (list $24.99) is the cheapest Qi2 charger here from a brand that publishes real certification. It delivers 15W magnetically to iPhone 12 and newer and to Qi2 Android phones, with foreign-object detection and over-current/over-voltage protection. UGREEN recommends a 25W or higher adapter — not included. For $13 more the Belkin pad doubles the wattage, so only buy this if your phone caps at 15W anyway. [ src10 , src11 ]
 Best 15W 3-in-1: Anker MagGo UFO 3-in-1 ($73.99) — Check price 
 Anker's baseball-sized foldable charges an iPhone 15 Pro to 20% in 15 minutes and an Apple Watch Series 9 to 30% in 22 minutes, supports StandBy mode when folded open, and — unusually at this price — ships with a travel case, a 40W adapter and a 5ft USB-C cable. At $73.99 (list $99.99) it is the sensible 15W 3-in-1 if your phone can't use 25W. [ src1 , src2 ]
 Best Travel: Twelve South ButterFly SE ($79.99) — Check price 
 Folding to 2.25 x 1 inches — about the size of an AirPods Pro case — the ButterFly SE is still the most compact multi-device charger available. It charges an iPhone (15W Qi2) and an Apple Watch simultaneously, doubles as a StandBy display stand and a Nightstand-mode watch pedestal, and can also charge AirPods Pro on the second pad instead of the watch [ src1 , src2 ]. The SE omits the bundled wall charger to hit its price; it is $79.99 in August (list $99.99). [ src1 ]
 Best Upright Stand: Mophie Snap+ 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Stand ($119.98) — Check price 
 Tom's Guide's long-standing top pick, the mophie 3-in-1 Extendable Stand, is no longer stocked on Amazon (mophie still sells it direct), so the live mophie pick is the Snap+ 3-in-1 stand: Qi2-certified and MagSafe-compatible at 15W for the phone, Apple Watch 0-80% in about 45 minutes, 5W for AirPods, an adjustable head for portrait or landscape viewing, and a wall charger in the box. mophie lists it at $129.95; Amazon shows $119.98 [ src1 , src12 ]. It is the pick if you want an upright, weighted stand at eye level for video calls rather than a folding travel puck. [ src12 ]
 Best for Car: ESR OmniLock Qi2.2 25W Car Mount ($56.99) — Check price 
 The OmniLock is a genuinely Qi2.2-certified 25W car charger with CryoBoost active cooling, N52 magnets and a reinforced aluminium vent hook with over-tightening protection — important because 25W in a hot car is exactly where thermal throttling bites [ src5 ]. Note the pick change: the iOttie Velox Pro that previously held this slot specifies only 7.5W MagSafe charging on its Amazon listing, so it does not belong on a Qi2 card. If you want maximum mount stability over maximum watts, iOttie's Velox Qi2 Mini ($54.95, Qi2-certified 15W with a 20W adapter included) is the alternative. [ src5 ]
 Best Wall Charger: Twelve South PowerBug ($49.99) — Check price 
 The PowerBug turns a wall outlet into a floating Qi2 charging dock: a 15W Qi2 magnetic pad plus a 35W USB-C PD port with PPS, sharing a 35W total budget (the wired port drops to 20W when both are in use). Prongs stow flat for travel and the pad supports StandBy mode. $49.99 in Slate or Dune. The Dune listing this card previously linked was delisted; the live ASIN is the Slate colorway. [ src1 ]
 Head-to-Head Comparisons
 ESR CryoBoost Foldable vs Belkin Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 Foldable
 Both are $99.99 25W Qi2.2 foldable 3-in-1s that charge an iPhone 0-50% in roughly 30 minutes and bundle a wall adapter (ESR 50W, Belkin 45W). The ESR runs an active CryoBoost fan that holds peak wattage longer; the Belkin uses ChillBoost passive cooling — silent, but it throttles sooner [ src2 , src6 , src8 ].
 Pick ESR CryoBoost if: you charge for long stretches, want sustained peak speed, and value the larger 50W bundled brick.
 Pick Belkin 3-in-1 if: you want silent operation and Belkin's warranty/retail support, and you're happy trading a few minutes of peak speed for no fan.
 Belkin Qi2.2 25W 2-in-1 ($59.99) vs Belkin Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 ($99.99)
 Same 25W speed, same 45W adapter, same folding design — the $40 difference buys the dedicated fast-charge Apple Watch puck. The 2-in-1 substitutes a 5W USB-C port, which will charge a watch overnight from your own cable but not at fast-charge rates [ src3 ].
 Pick the 2-in-1 if: you don't own an Apple Watch, or you already carry its magnetic cable — it is the best value 25W charger on this card.
 Pick the 3-in-1 if: you want Apple Watch Series 10 fast charging (0-80% in 30 minutes) without carrying a second cable.
 ESR CryoBoost vs Anker Prime 3-in-1
 Both are premium actively cooled 25W Qi2.2 foldables. Anker's AirCool is quieter (19 dB rated) and adds a smart status display and pop-out Watch dock; ESR is $20 cheaper and folds thinner, with a 50W brick included [ src1 , src5 , src6 ].
 Pick ESR CryoBoost if: travel bulk and price matter — $99.99 vs $119.99 for effectively the same charging speed.
 Pick Anker Prime if: you want the quietest fan, the charging display, and Anker's ecosystem/warranty, and the $20 premium is immaterial.
 Belkin Qi2 25W Pad ($29.99) vs UGREEN Qi2 15W Pad ($16.99)
 The cheapest single-device options. Belkin delivers the full 25W Qi2.2 to iPhone 17 (and iPhone 16 on iOS 26), Galaxy S26 Ultra or Pixel 10 Pro XL and adds a kickstand and a tethered 6.6ft cable; UGREEN is a plain Qi2 15W pad at $16.99 [ src3 , src10 , src11 ].
 Pick Belkin 25W if: you own a 25W-capable phone — the extra $13 roughly halves the time to 50%, provided you feed it a 30W+ adapter.
 Pick UGREEN 15W if: your phone caps at 15W (iPhone 12-16 on iOS 18, base Galaxy S26, most Android) — the 25W pad would give you nothing extra.
 Belkin Qi2.2 3-in-1 for Android ($64.95) vs UGREEN MagFlow ($139.99)
 Two 25W multi-device options at very different prices. The Belkin is built around Android watch pucks — you supply your own watch charger, which is why it is $75 cheaper; the UGREEN is a complete foldable stand with tilt/rotation, 16 magnets and a bundled adapter [ src3 , src7 ].
 Pick the Belkin Android station if: you already own your smartwatch's charger and want 25W phone + earbuds charging for under $70.
 Pick UGREEN MagFlow if: you want one box that charges everything with no extra parts, need the tilt/rotate stand for StandBy or FaceTime, and can catch it below list.
 Decision Logic
 If budget < $20
 → UGREEN Qi2 15W Pad ($16.99). The cheapest Qi2-certified pad from a brand that publishes certification, now that ESR's HaloLock Mini line is out of stock on Amazon US. Single device only, no adapter included. Avoid sub-$15 unbranded "Qi2 certified" pads — verify certification on the WPC database or the maker's spec sheet. [ src10 , src11 ]
 If budget is $20-$60
 → Spigen Foldable Qi2.2 2-in-1 ($24.99) for the cheapest full 25W, Belkin Qi2 25W Magnetic Pad ($29.99) for a single-device pad with a kickstand, Twelve South PowerBug ($49.99) for a wall-plug charger, or the Belkin Qi2.2 25W 2-in-1 Foldable ($59.99) if you want the best all-round value with a 45W adapter in the box. [ src2 , src3 ]
 If user wants fastest possible charging (25W Qi2.2)
 → ESR CryoBoost Foldable 3-in-1 ($99.99) for actively cooled multi-device, or Belkin Qi2.2 25W 2-in-1 ($59.99) if you only need the phone at full speed. Requires iPhone 17 (or iPhone 16 on iOS 26), Galaxy S26 Ultra, or Pixel 10 Pro XL, plus a 30W+ USB-C PD adapter. Active cooling sustains peak speeds longer than passive. [ src3 , src5 , src6 ]
 If user needs iPhone + Apple Watch + AirPods charging
 → ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 ($99.99) or Belkin Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 Foldable ($99.99) for 25W with a real MFW watch puck; Anker Prime ($119.99) for the quietest fan plus a display; Anker MagGo UFO ($73.99) if 15W is enough. Skip Belkin's 15W BoostCharge Pro at $89.99 — it costs almost as much as the 25W model. [ src2 , src3 , src8 ]
 If user is on Samsung or Android
 → Belkin Qi2.2 25W 3-in-1 for Android ($64.95), but budget for your own watch puck (not included) and a Qi2-compliant magnetic case up to 3mm. Only the Galaxy S26 Ultra and Pixel 10 Pro XL take the full 25W; the base S26 is capped at 15W. [ src3 , src7 ]
 If user travels frequently
 → Twelve South ButterFly SE ($79.99), which folds to 2.25 x 1 inches for iPhone + Watch. For a 3-in-1 that still packs flat, ESR CryoBoost folds to 0.62 inches thick, and the Belkin Qi2.2 2-in-1 ($59.99) is the cheapest folding 25W option. [ src1 , src2 , src3 ]
 If user needs a car mount charger
 → ESR OmniLock Qi2.2 25W Car Mount ($56.99) with CryoBoost cooling and an aluminium vent hook. Choose iOttie's Velox Qi2 Mini ($54.95, 15W, 20W adapter included) if mount stability outranks wattage. Do not buy the 7.5W iOttie Velox Pro expecting Qi2 speeds. [ src5 ]
 Default recommendation
 → ESR CryoBoost Foldable 3-in-1 ($99.99): 25W Qi2.2, active cooling, folds for travel, 50W charger in the box, charges iPhone + Watch + AirPods. If the budget matters more than the Watch puck, the Belkin Qi2.2 25W 2-in-1 Foldable ($59.99) delivers the same phone charging speed for $40 less. [ src2 , src3 , src5 , src6 ]
 Key Market Trends (Q3 2026)
 25W is now cheaper than 15W used to be: Belkin's Qi2.2 25W 2-in-1 sits at $59.99, its 25W Android 3-in-1 at $64.95, and Spigen's 25W 2-in-1 at $24.99 — while Belkin's own 15W BoostCharge Pro 3-in-1 rose to $89.99 and Satechi's 15W Trio holds at $129.99. Paying a premium for a 15W multi-device station no longer makes sense. [ src3 ]
 Spring sale prices reverted, hard: the UGREEN MagFlow was $99.99 in June and is $139.99 in August (+40%), matching Engadget's stated $140. Anything bought at a sale price in this category should be re-checked before citing it as the value pick. [ src3 ]
 iOS 26 is a gate on 25W: Belkin now states in its Qi2.2 listings that 25W wireless charging works only on iOS 26 and newer. An iPhone 16 held back on iOS 18 charges at 15W no matter which certified charger it sits on. [ src3 ]
 Certification noise is rising at the bottom of the market: Amazon searches for cheap Qi2 pads increasingly surface unbranded multi-packs claiming "Qi2 certified" at $8-10. The WPC's certification database and the manufacturer's own spec sheet are the only reliable checks — magnets alone are not Qi2. [ src11 ]
 ESR's budget pads went out of stock: the HaloLock Qi2 Mini and its kickstand and standard siblings are all listed "currently unavailable" on Amazon US as of 2026-08-05, leaving UGREEN's $16.99 pad and IKEA's $9.99 Västmärke donut as the cheap Qi2 options. [ src9 , src10 ]
 Galaxy S26 keeps Qi2 but still no built-in magnets: the S26 Ultra supports 25W Qi2, but the whole S26 line needs a magnetic case for alignment (Samsung cites that 83% of users already use cases), and the base S26 is limited to 15W. [ src7 ]
 Qi2.2 device expansion: iPhone 17, Pixel 10 Pro XL and Galaxy S26 Ultra now take 25W; the WPC's roadmap allows for higher ceilings in future Qi revisions. [ src4 , src11 ]
 IKEA's $9.99 Qi2 donut still undercuts everyone: IKEA's three Qi2-certified Västmärke chargers (donut pad $9.99, stand $24.99, lit bowl $24.99) remain the cheapest mainstream-brand Qi2 hardware, all 15W and IKEA-exclusive. [ src9 ]
 Important Caveats
 Prices are US Amazon prices verified on 2026-08-05 and move frequently. This category swings 30-40% between sale and list — the UGREEN MagFlow moved from $99.99 to $139.99 and the Belkin 15W 3-in-1 from $66.49 to $89.99 in five weeks. Re-check before buying.
 25W charging requires a Qi2.2-certified charger AND a compatible device (iPhone 17 series, iPhone 16 on iOS 26 or newer, Galaxy S26 Ultra, Pixel 10 Pro XL) AND a 30W+ USB-C PD adapter. Older devices max out at 15W or 7.5W regardless of charger.
 Power adapters are frequently NOT included. The Belkin 25W pad, the UGREEN 15W pad, the Spigen 2-in-1 and the Twelve South ButterFly SE all ship without a brick; the ESR CryoBoost (50W), Belkin foldables (45W), UGREEN MagFlow and Anker MagGo UFO (40W) do include one. Add $20-30 where it is missing.
 Belkin's 25W 3-in-1 for Android includes a watch cradle but no watch charger — you insert your own Samsung, Google or Apple puck. Price that in.
 Real-world sustained speeds are below peak 25W due to thermal throttling; active cooling (ESR CryoBoost, Anker AirCool at 19 dB) extends the fast window rather than removing the limit. Passively cooled units may hold 25W for only 5-10 minutes.
 Samsung Galaxy S25/S26 need a compatible magnetic case for Qi2 alignment; without one, charging works but alignment is manual and speeds are inconsistent.
 Apple Watch fast charging requires an MFW-certified (Made for Watch) module; not every third-party station includes one.
 "Qi2 certified", "Qi2 Ready" and "MagSafe compatible" are three different claims. Only Qi2/Qi2.2 certification is verifiable through the Wireless Power Consortium; treat unbranded listings that claim certification without a WPC entry as unverified.
 Two previously listed picks are no longer buyable on Amazon US: the ESR HaloLock Qi2 Mini and the mophie 3-in-1 Extendable Stand (mophie still sells the Extendable direct at mophie.com). This card links their live replacements.
 This comparison covers stationary, wall and car chargers. Qi2 power banks are covered in the portable chargers card.

 Apple’s MagSafe Charger reaches up to 25W on iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max with a 30W or greater adapter. iPhone Air peaks at 20W, and iPhone 17e stops at 15W. The certified pads in this guide are Qi2 15W products, trading speed for a much lower price.

 iPhone Air peaks at 20W, iPhone 16 and iPhone 16 Pro peak at 22.5W, and iPhone 17e plus iPhone 15 and earlier sit in the 15W tier

 Plug USB-C or Lightning headphones in while charging wirelessly and the ceiling drops to 10W on 17 Pro and 17 Pro Max, or 16W on iPhone 17 and iPhone Air

 # What Charging Speeds Does iPhone 17 Actually Get Over MagSafe?
 iPhone 17 supports three wireless tiers, and the pad you buy decides which one you actually see.
 Standard iPhone 17 is a 25W phone, not a 15W one. That correction matters, because plenty of buying advice still puts the non-Pro model a full tier below its siblings.
 According to Apple’s MagSafe support article , the charger “intelligently adapts to conditions to optimize charging your iPhone at up to 25W of peak power delivery.” The puck negotiates that speed in real time with the phone and the adapter, so any weak link throttles the whole stack.
 Apple publishes the ceiling per model, and it’s not a clean split between Pro and non-Pro.

 MagSafe peak wireless watts by iPhone model, per Apple Support 105047. 
 Two rows surprise people. iPhone Air, despite launching alongside the 17 line, peaks at 20W rather than 25W. And iPhone 16 Plus and 16 Pro Max reach the full 25W while the smaller iPhone 16 and 16 Pro stop at 22.5W.
 The 25W row also carries a hardware condition most roundups skip. Apple names four charger part numbers for that tier: A3502, A3503, A2580, or A3250 , printed on the puck or its cable. An older A2140 puck tops out at 15W no matter which phone or brick you attach.
 The MagSafe spec covers iPhone 12 through iPhone 17. Older Qi-only pads (the kind sold for iPhone 8 through iPhone 11) physically work, but they cap at 7.5W with no magnetic alignment. Our best wireless charger for iPhone 11 breakdown covers that older Qi tier.
 Certification, not “MagSafe-compatible” marketing copy, is what sets a third-party pad’s tier. Both Anker pads in this guide are Qi2 15W.
 Wattage is a peak, not an average. Charging tapers as the battery fills or the phone warms, so nobody sees 25W for a whole session.
 # MagSafe 25W vs Qi2 25W: What the Names Actually Mean
 They’re the same 25W ceiling reached two ways, and the naming confusion is the reason shoppers overpay.
 Apple’s language is narrow. According to Apple’s iPhone charge speeds page , “for faster wireless charging, use a MagSafe Charger or a Qi2-certified wireless charger.” Apple names exactly two things: its own MagSafe Charger, and Qi2 certification.
 The third-party side changed names mid-flight. 9to5Mac reported in its coverage of the standard’s launch that “the WPC originally referred to the latest standard as Qi 2.2, but has now decided that it’s clearer to include the power rating in the name.” The official name is now Qi2 25W .
 So “Qi2.2” is a retired internal version label, not a product tier and not an Apple term. Listings still using it are describing Qi2 25W.
 That leaves three real tiers to shop against: Qi at 7.5W, Qi2 15W, and Qi2 25W. The two Anker picks below are Qi2 15W, which is why they undercut Apple’s puck on price and sit below it on speed.
 # Best MagSafe Charger Overall: Apple MagSafe Charger (1 m)
 Apple’s own MagSafe puck is the only pad here that ships with a full Apple warranty, an official up-to-25W iPhone 17 rating, and a 1 m attached USB-C cable that fits modern AppleCare repair paths. Check the part number before you buy: the 25W tier needs A3502, A3503, A2580, or A3250.  Two trade-offs to know.
 First, the adapter isn’t in the box. You’ll need a 20W or higher USB-C PD brick (our GaN charger for iPhone 16 roundup covers cheap fast bricks that pair well).
 Second, the magnets are slightly weaker than Apple’s puck. The phone lifts off with one finger, where Apple’s puck holds tighter and needs a more deliberate pull.

 # Best Single-Pad MagSafe Stand: Anker MagGo Qi2 Stand

 # Apple vs Qi2 Third-Party for iPhone 17
 The charging ceiling depends on both phone and charger. A current-part Apple puck reaches 25W on iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max; the Anker pads here are Qi2 15W products. Warranty, magnet strength, and price still separate the choices.
